evidence: Cic. Leg. 2.15: piōrum et impiōrum habēre ratiōnem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “that performs what is due to the gods and religion in general, to parents, kindred … pious, devout, conscientious, affectionate”. Not only towards God: a dutiful son is pius too. The superlative piissimus is post-Augustan; Cicero called it no Latin at all (Phil. 13.43).
Of persons, devout and careful in worship, and so scrupulous, conscientious; of places and things, sacred, or under a ban (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Religiōsior tū quidem es, quam prō aetāte. — Immō nūllam aetātem nōn decet religiō.
phrases.english: “You are very devout for your age.” — “But there is no age that devotion does not suit.”
(that the gods) take account of the devout and the ungodly
